businessModel: Free tier; Premium subscription (first-month discount code SIGMA50 advertised)
paidNote: Premium subscription; prices not stated on home page
updateCadence: Unclear; Windows build on older Chromium than macOS
summary: Chromium browser from an Estonian company with an on-device LLM (Eclipse), an AI agent, chat with page and Deep Research. Windows, macOS, iOS; Android in waitlist. Marketing-heavy, little independent testing.
bestFor: People who want offline/local AI in a browser
Privacy-leaning users who accept unverified claims
Windows/macOS users wanting a free AI browser
notFor: Users who need fast Chromium patching
Anyone wanting a mature mobile app

pros.title: Local LLM
pros.detail: Eclipse runs on-device so supported prompts need no cloud processing.

pros.title: Four-platform footprint
pros.detail: Windows, macOS, iOS apps plus an Android waitlist/APK.

pros.title: Built-in ad blocker
pros.detail: Advertised ad blocker with no extension needed.

pros.title: Free tier includes AI
pros.detail: Free plan covers Eclipse, Chat with Page and limited Agent and Deep Research.

cons.title: Unverified privacy claims
cons.detail: E2EE, SOC 2 and open-source statements are vendor marketing only.

cons.title: Chromium lag
cons.detail: Windows installer was on Chromium 149 while the macOS build was on 152.

cons.title: Thin independent reviews
cons.detail: TechArcade notes few ratings (iOS 3.4 stars from 7) and little testing.

cons.title: Local AI is slower
cons.detail: On-device answers are slower on weak hardware.

faq.a: Eclipse is described as an on-device LLM; the underlying model and requirements are not named.
The vendor says its code is open source, but we could not confirm a public repository.
Linux is "coming soon"; Android is a waitlist with a 1.0.1 APK.

timeline.event: Sigma AI Browser launches (exact date unverified)
Site lists Windows, macOS (incl. Mac App Store) and iOS downloads; Android waitlist
Site offers Android APK 1.0.1 via waitlist dialog

spec.patchLag: Windows build 3 Chromium majors behind macOS build on the site

jsSpeed: Blink/V8 engine, Chrome-class JS speed; no vendor benchmark
pageLoad: Chromium rendering; AI sidebar adds overhead
networkSpeed: Chromium network stack with HTTP/3 and preloading
startup: Chromium cold start, heavier than plain Chrome
memory: Chromium multi-process plus AI layer; RAM-heavy
cpu: Chromium-class; agent tasks add background load
lowEnd: Needs modern hardware; AI features add load
installSize: Full Chromium bundle, a few hundred MB
privacyDefaults: Local LLM and ad blocker, but claims unverified
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox but patching lag on Windows
patchSpeed: Windows build 3 Chromium majors behind macOS build
behaviourCustom: Few shortcut or per-site options documented
tabManagement: Tab groups and search; no workspaces documented
searchFreedom: Default search changeable; AI prompt flow is the focus
productivity: AI sidebar, page chat and summaries
translation: AI-driven page translation; no dedicated engine
extras: Local LLM, ad blocker, Deep Research
extensions: Chrome Web Store but MV3 only since the Aug 2026 MV2 purge
mobileApps: iOS app with few ratings; Android only waitlist
accessibility: Chromium accessibility stack, unverified for AI layer
longevity: Small vendor; active builds on site
ai: Local LLM plus agent; agent quality rated average
